modules.summary: Models the Knudson route from a constitutional heterozygous tumour-suppressor lesion, through a somatic second hit, to biallelic loss, clonal initiation and the early-onset/multifocal/bilateral clinical signature. The chain is linear, correctly directed and historically well sourced (Knudson 1971, Cavenee 1983, TCGA germline pan-cancer), the classical and continuum models are curated as competing hypotheses rather than one being asserted, and the notes are unusually careful about what a conformer must not copy (proto-oncogene syndromes, unproven second hits, the Lynch-only aspirin evidence). It is the batch's most-used module (113 links from 43 files). What needs attention is anchoring: the GO terms on the first-hit and second-hit nodes name one specific mechanism each, and almost every conformer diverges from them, so conformance can barely be checked at the two nodes most conformers attach to.
strengths: Hypothesis groups make the biallelic-vs-haploinsufficiency question explicit instead of asserting complete second hits.
Treatment carries an explicit CRITICAL scope caveat that conformers do not inherit the aspirin recommendation.
The tissue-selectivity knowledge gap honestly records what the two-hit model cannot predict.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Somatic Second-Hit Inactivation of the Wild-Type Allele].biological_processes
findings.quote: Interstitial deletion, an independent intragenic point mutation, and promoter hypermethylation (an epigenetic second hit) are the other recognized routes.
findings.problem: The node's only bound process is GO:0006312 mitotic recombination with modifier INCREASED, while the node's own description lists four routes to the second hit (nondisjunction, mitotic recombination, interstitial deletion, intragenic point mutation, promoter hypermethylation). Two things follow. First, the modifier asserts that mitotic recombination is increased, which is not the claim: in most predisposition syndromes the recombination rate is normal and what matters is that one such event happened at that locus. Second, the single mechanism-specific term leaves the other three routes unrepresentable, which is why 27 of the 28 conformer links into this node are process_absent - the two conformers I opened (an APC somatic point mutation in Classic_Familial_Adenomatous_Polyposis, PRKAR1A loss of heterozygosity in Carney_Complex) describe deletion/point mutation/LOH and bind no mitotic-recombination term. This is the 'most conformers diverge' case the review protocol treats as a lead about the module rather than about the conformers.
findings.suggestion: Either drop the modifier to a direction-agnostic value and state in the node description that the bound term names only the canonical LOH route, or replace it with a term that covers the claim the node actually makes (loss of heterozygosity / biallelic inactivation) and move mitotic recombination into the prose list of routes. I did not find a GO term for loss of heterozygosity and am not suggesting a specific replacement CURIE unverified.
findings.verification: Read the module in full; confirmed GO:0006312 label 'mitotic recombination' in cache/go/terms.csv; opened the second-hit conformer nodes in kb/disorders/Classic_Familial_Adenomatous_Polyposis.yaml and kb/disorders/Carney_Complex.yaml; fact sheet gives 27/28 process_absent at this node.

findings.quote: the mismatch-repair genes MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/ PMS2 (Lynch syndrome), BRCA1/BRCA2 (hereditary breast and ovarian cancer), VHL (von Hippel-Lindau)
findings.problem: The first-hit node binds GO:0008285 negative regulation of cell population proliferation (DECREASED) as the single process standing for 'tumour suppressor function lost'. For a large part of the gene list in the module's own notes that is not the gene's function: MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2 are mismatch repair, BRCA1/BRCA2/PALB2 homologous recombination, FH and SDHx TCA-cycle enzymes, FLCN a nutrient-sensing regulator. The term therefore functions as a label for 'tumour suppressor' rather than as a checkable claim about the node, and 36 of 37 conformer links into it are process_absent - the module's most-used node is also the one a conformer can least be compared against.
findings.suggestion: State in the notes that the proliferation-restraint term is a stand-in and that a conformer is expected to bind its own gene's function instead, so the divergence is documented rather than looking like a defect; or split the trigger into the two or three functional classes the gene list really contains (growth-restraint, DNA-repair, metabolic) so that conformance has something to check.
findings.verification: Read module in full; confirmed GO:0008285 label in cache/go/terms.csv; counted the gene classes in the module's own notes; conformer counts from the batch fact sheet. Rests on my own reading of those genes' functions rather than a fetched source.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Early-Onset, Multifocal, and Bilateral Tumor Spectrum]
findings.quote: The clinical signature of the module and the basis on which hereditary predisposition is recognized before any gene is sequenced
findings.problem: The consequence node binds no ontology term at all, so all 11 conformer links into it are anchor_no_process: the module's clinical-signature node cannot be compared with a conformer's. This is partly irreducible (there is no GO process for a tumour spectrum), but the module does not say so, and a curator reading the conformance report sees 11 unexplained anchor_no_process links.
findings.suggestion: Record in the node description or the module notes that this node is deliberately unbound because the claim is epidemiological rather than a cellular process, so the anchor_no_process links read as intended rather than as a gap.
findings.verification: Re-read the node in the file: it has description, role, biological_scale and evidence but no biological_processes, cell_types or locations block. Fact sheet reports anchor_no_process=11.

modules.summary: Models the oncometabolite route: a metabolic enzyme lesion raises fumarate, succinate or R-2-hydroxyglutarate to concentrations at which they competitively inhibit 2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, with three evidenced downstream branches (HIF stabilisation, TET/Jumonji inhibition and hypermethylation, and fumarate-specific KEAP1 succination). The biology is accurate and well sourced to the founding papers, the branch controversy is curated as three hypothesis groups plus a CONTROVERSY and a HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion, and the notes correctly forbid an SDHx or IDH conformer from attaching to the succination branch. The weakness is at the two top nodes: the trigger bundles two genetically opposite lesions and binds terms for only one of them, and the accumulation node's TCA-cycle term contradicts the module's own 'not an energetic deficit' framing.
strengths: Three competing drivers are curated as hypothesis groups on the edges rather than one being asserted.
The HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH discussion names exactly which load-bearing claims are mouse- or cell-derived.
Notes state the genetic-architecture difference between the TCA-suppressor and IDH routes, including that the IDH route must not be curated as needing a second hit.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Metabolic Enzyme Lesion (TCA Tumor Suppressor Loss or IDH Neomorphic Gain)].molecular_functions
findings.quote: The initiating lesion, reached by two opposite genetic routes.
findings.problem: The trigger node is one node carrying two mechanistically opposite lesions (biallelic loss of a TCA enzyme; heterozygous neomorphic gain at IDH1/IDH2), and its only bound functions are fumarate hydratase activity (GO:0004333, DECREASED) and succinate dehydrogenase activity (GO:0008177, DECREASED). Nothing on the node represents the IDH arm, yet four of the five conformer links the fact sheet lists at this node are IDH entries (Diffuse_Astrocytoma, IDH_Mutant_Astrocytoma, IDH_Mutant_Cholangiocarcinoma, IDH_Mutant_Oligodendroglioma), and all six links are process_absent. An IDH conformer attaching here is being checked against two enzyme activities its disease does not lose, and the DECREASED modifiers assert loss where the IDH lesion is a gain of a new activity.
findings.suggestion: Either bind the IDH arm on the same node - GO:0004450 isocitrate dehydrogenase (NADP+) activity is the term for IDH1/IDH2, confirmed in cache/go/terms.csv, though note the claim there is a neomorphic gain and partial loss of normal activity rather than simple DECREASED - or split the trigger into two sibling nodes (TCA suppressor loss; IDH neomorphic gain) that both feed Oncometabolite Accumulation, which would also let the two routes carry their own genetic-architecture caveats.
findings.verification: Re-read the trigger node in the file; confirmed GO:0004333, GO:0008177, GO:0004450 and GO:0004449 labels in cache/go/terms.csv; conformer list and process_absent=6 from the batch fact sheet.

findings.quote: the resulting loss of dioxygenase activity — not any energetic deficit — is what drives tumorigenesis
findings.problem: The accumulation node's only bound process is GO:0006099 tricarboxylic acid cycle with modifier DECREASED. That is not the node's claim - the node asserts that a specific metabolite reaches inhibitory concentration - and it works against the module's own framing, quoted here, that the mechanism is a signalling lesion and not a TCA/energetic deficit. It is also false for one of the module's two routes: mutant IDH1 is cytosolic, the wild-type allele is retained, and 2-HG accumulation does not require reduced TCA flux. The term reads as 'this is a TCA disease', which is the reading the description exists to rule out.
findings.suggestion: Replace or supplement it with a term for the metabolite-level claim at this node, or drop the process binding and carry the accumulation in prose plus the chemistry (the module already keeps chemistry in prose by convention), noting in the description that the TCA lesion applies only to the FH/SDHx arm. I have not verified a specific replacement CURIE, so treat any suggested term as unverified.
findings.verification: Re-read the node and the module description; confirmed GO:0006099 label in cache/go/terms.csv; the quoted span is from the module's own description.

findings.location: pathophysiology[KEAP1 Succination and NRF2 Antioxidant Pathway Activation].role
findings.problem: The succination branch is given role adaptive_escape, but the module presents it as a third parallel driver branch of the lesion (its own hypothesis group, nrf2_succination_driver, is a candidate oncogenic driver, and the mouse genetics is cited as evidence that it, not HIF, drives FH-associated disease). adaptive_escape suggests escape from a stress or a therapy, which is what the role means in the batch's resistance modules. The other two branches of the same parent node are role effector.
findings.suggestion: Change the role to effector, matching the two sibling branches it runs in parallel with, and keep the fumarate-specificity caveat where it already is in the description and notes.
findings.verification: Re-read the node, its hypothesis group and the two sibling effector branches in the file. Role semantics inferred from use across this batch rather than from a schema definition of adaptive_escape.

modules.summary: Models ligand-independent Hedgehog activation from loss of pathway restraint through constitutive SMO activity and constitutive GLI output to Hedgehog-driven proliferation, and defines the SMO-inhibitor drug-target pattern. Direction, drug target and the SUFU/GLI2 bypass are all handled correctly, and the description draws a clear boundary against the loss-of-signal developmental Hedgehog disorders. Two things weaken it: the trigger node is named and bound for loss of negative regulation but is also where activating SMO lesions are filed, and the GLI node binds the same smoothened-signalling term as the SMO node it is explicitly independent of, so the two nodes are not distinguishable by their anchors.
strengths: The SMO-independent bypass (SUFU loss, GLI2 amplification) is modelled as a separate edge from the trigger and tied to SMO-inhibitor resistance.
Notes separate the gene-level direction (LOSS_OF_FUNCTION vs GAIN_OF_FUNCTION) from the pathway-level direction, which is always activation.

findings.location: pathophysiology[Loss of Hedgehog Pathway Negative Regulation]
findings.quote: loss-of-function of a negative regulator (biallelic/Knudson two-hit inactivation of the tumor suppressors PTCH1, PTCH2, or SUFU) OR gain-of-function of the positive transducer SMO (activating mutation)
findings.problem: The node's name and its single bound process (GO:0045879 negative regulation of smoothened signaling pathway, DECREASED) describe only the first of the two lesions its own description calls 'mechanistically opposite'. An activating SMO mutation is a gain in the positive transducer, not a decrease in negative regulation, and Basal_Cell_Carcinoma#SMO Activating Mutations conforms at this node, so a gain-of-function lesion is recorded under a loss-of-negative-regulation claim with a DECREASED modifier. A curator reading the node name alone would not file an SMO mutation here, and one reading the bound term would conclude the module asserts reduced PTCH/SUFU restraint in SMO-mutant disease.
findings.suggestion: Rename the node to cover both routes (for example 'Loss of Pathway Restraint or Activating SMO Lesion') and say in the description which bound term applies to which route; or split the SMO-activating lesion onto its own trigger node feeding Constitutive Smoothened Activity directly.
findings.verification: Re-read the node, its term block and the module notes; the SMO-mutation conformer link at this node is listed in the batch fact sheet; confirmed GO:0045879 label in cache/go/terms.csv.

findings.quote: it is the SMO-independent convergence point that underlies both SUFU-driven disease and acquired resistance to SMO inhibitors
findings.problem: This node is declared the SMO-independent convergence point, yet its first bound process is GO:0007224 smoothened signaling pathway (INCREASED) - the same single term, with the same modifier, as the Constitutive Smoothened Activity node above it. The two nodes are therefore indistinguishable by their anchors, which both weakens conformance checking (a conformer binding the smoothened term matches either node equally) and sits oddly beside a description whose point is that GLI output continues when SMO signalling is blocked.
findings.suggestion: Drop GO:0007224 from this node and let the transcriptional term (GO:0045944) carry it, or add a GLI-specific term if one exists - I did not look one up, so treat that half of the suggestion as unverified.
findings.verification: Re-read both node term blocks in the file; confirmed GO:0007224 and GO:0045879 labels in cache/go/terms.csv.

modules.summary: Models sustained nuclear sex-steroid receptor signalling expanding a hormone-responsive tissue, with a benign proliferative lesion as the usual endpoint. The chain is correctly directed, the boundary against sustaining_proliferative_signaling is stated precisely (intact ligand-dependent receptor here, ligand-independent activation there, with ESR1-mutant endocrine resistance explicitly handed over), and the module is unusually honest about its own anchoring - it records that the trigger node is realised as environmental edges and that the declared key conformance target currently has one conformer. The defect is in the second treatment, which makes a progestin-protective claim at a module-level node that the module's own notes say is progesterone-driven in two of its conformers.
strengths: The notes state the module/sibling boundary as a test a curator can apply, including when a conformer has left the module.
The node descriptions record where conformers attach and why, rather than implying the declared key target is the most-used one.
Explicitly declines an Xogenesis anchor and says why the terminal output is too heterogeneous in form for one.

findings.location: treatments[Progestin Opposition of the Target Tissue].target_mechanisms
findings.quote: Restoring progestin opposition prevents formation of the benign proliferative lesion that is this module's usual endpoint.
findings.problem: The progestin treatment's target_mechanisms edge says INHIBITS against the module-level node Benign Hormone-Dependent Proliferative Lesion, i.e. a claim about every conformer that reaches that node. But the module's own notes say the myometrial conformer runs on progesterone receptor signalling (GO:0050847) rather than oestrogen - 'note this conformer runs on progesterone rather than oestrogen' - and the amplifier node lists breast fibroadenoma alongside leiomyoma as MED12-mutant mesenchymal conformers. For those tissues progesterone is a driver of the lesion, not the opposing signal, and Breast_Fibroadenoma is one of the three conformers at the very node this edge targets. The treatment description does scope the claim to the endometrium, but the structured edge does not, so the module asserts at graph level that progestin inhibits a lesion it elsewhere says progesterone drives.
findings.suggestion: Retarget the edge at the oestrogen-driven route rather than the shared consequence node (for example at the amplifier node with the endometrial scope stated), or keep the target and add the scope to the target_mechanisms description plus a sentence in the notes that this treatment pattern is not inherited by the progesterone-driven mesenchymal conformers - the same CRITICAL-scope-caveat device the other modules in this batch use for their treatments.
findings.verification: Re-read both treatments, the amplifier node description and the notes in the file; conformer list at the consequence node (Breast_Fibroadenoma, Endometrial_Carcinoma, Endometrial_Endometrioid_Adenocarcinoma) from the batch fact sheet; confirmed GO:0050847 is cited in the module's own notes for the myometrial substitution.
